title: School-run parking in Rochdale: what can the council do?
excerpt: The council has stepped up patrols outside schools and is consulting on School Streets. New pavement parking powers are on the way from the government.
body:
Parents across the borough who face double-parked cars, blocked crossings and mounted pavements at the school gates every morning have more options than they may think.

Rochdale Borough Council launched its Stop Means Stop campaign at St Luke's Primary School in Heywood on 28 September, telling drivers to stop for school crossing patrols.

The council recorded 137 cases over the past five years of drivers failing to stop outside schools, including cases where a crossing patrol had already stepped into the road.

It said parking enforcement patrols outside schools would increase, with no fixed schedule, and asked drivers to keep yellow lines and school keep-clear markings free.

Councillor Dylan Williams, cabinet member for highways and facilities, said: “It's really important that people stop.” He described the risk as “a real danger for schoolchildren across the borough.”

A crossing patrol worker at St Luke's said cars parked on the zigzag lines blocked his view and the view of passing drivers.

One longer-term answer is a School Street. These schemes restrict vehicles on the road outside a school at drop-off and pick-up times, so it becomes a space for people walking, cycling or scooting.

Residents, Blue Badge holders, healthcare workers and the emergency services can be given exemptions, according to the council. A School Street can only go ahead with the school's backing, and schools or communities register interest through Transport for Greater Manchester.

The council has consulted on a School Street trial at Smithy Bridge Primary School in Littleborough, with a consultation that ran from 27 November 2025 to 16 January 2026. No decision has been published.

Pavement parking is the other common complaint. On 8 January, the Department for Transport announced that councils in England would get powers to restrict pavement parking across wider areas, rather than street by street.

Local transport minister Lilian Greenwood said: “Clear pavements are essential for people to move around safely and independently.” The department said guidance on using the powers would be published later in 2026.

Since July 2023 the council has also held powers to fine drivers caught on camera committing moving traffic offences, such as blocking yellow box junctions and making banned turns.

Problem parking outside a school can be reported to the council's Parking Services at ParkingServices@rochdale.gov.uk or on 0300 303 8879, Monday to Friday, 8.30am to 4.45pm. Dangerous driving should be reported to Greater Manchester Police on 101 or online, or 999 in an emergency.

Sources: Rochdale Borough Council; Department for Transport. Photograph: Rochdale Daily library.
